newsitem.title: USA: AMR reports drop in profits, cites labor pact.
newsitem.headline: AMR reports drop in profits, cites labor pact.

text.p: American Airlines' parent AMR Corp. Wednesday reported 3 percent lower first-quarter profits, which still topped Wall Street expectations, and cited a labour dispute with pilots at the nation's No. 2 airline.

"Despite the effects of a threatened pilot strike, strong levels of demand, combined with relatively limited capacity additions, produced good results for us," AMR Chairman Robert Crandall said in a statement.
"While our results are testimony to the continuing strength of demand, they would have been dramatically better absent the labour dispute," Crandall said.

AMR, which also saw fuel costs and operating expenses rise in the quarter, posted quarterly net income of $152 million, or $1.65 per share, compared with $157 million, or $2.02 per share, in the 1996 quarter.
The results included a $20 million pretax charge for stock options awarded to American's pilots as part of a tentative labour pact reached two weeks ago after months of bitter negotiations.
The results handily beat Wall Street expectations of $1.47 per share, and AMR stock climbed $2.125 to $84.75 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Operating revenues rose to $4.4 billion from $4.3 billion a year ago.

The labour pact, if approved by the pilots unions' members, averts the prospect of a second strike. On Feb. 15, the pilots went on strike, but they were sent almost immediately back to work by a Presidential Emergency Board created by President Clinton to resolve the dispute.
Although the strike was brief, American suffered as passengers booked flights on other airlines to avoid being stranded by the walkout.
AMR said American Airlines' fuel cost increased 16.9 percent to 74.7 cents a gallon. AMR's total aircraft fuel expenses were $520 million in the first quarter up from $441 million last year.
AMR's total operating expenses were $3.7 billion in the first quarter, up from $3.6 billion last year.
American Airlines is the No. 2 U.S. airline after United Airlines.
